the pst operon in B. subtilis encodes a phosphate-specific ABC-type transporter; the transcription of the pst genes is regulated in response to inorganic phosphate availability; and the transcription of the operon is processed in a manner that maintains a higher concentration of PstS mRNA than other components of the phosphate transporter
the pst operon encoding the high-affinity phosphate-specific ABC transporter is differentially processed to maintain high concentrations of PstA and PstS relative PstB and PstC.
the pst operon of B. subtilis is transcribed as a single unit but is differentially processed post-transcriptionally to maintain higher levels of PstS mRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the phosphate starvation response in Bacillus subtils.
the regulation of the pst operons in B. subtilis, and has identified the pstS gene as a key component in the regulation of the phosphate starvation response
the regulation of the phosphate-specific ABC-type transporter of Bacillus subtilus, and in particular the differential processing of its primary mRNA transcript.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pst operon in B. subtilis is transcribed as a single unit and is subject to differential mRNA processing.
pstS is transcribed from its own promoter, pstS is translocated to the cell surface and is processed from the primary transcript of pstS, pstA, pstB, pstC, and pstD.
PstS, which has a high affinity for inorganic phosphate, is the first component to be synthesized in response to phosphate starvation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pstS transcription is induced during phosphate starvation, but the pst operon transcript is differentially regulated at the post-transcriptional level.

the pst operon of B. subtilis is subject to post-transcriptional regulation, which involves differential processing of the primary mRNA transcript and that the differential regulation of the pst operons is important for the efficient uptake of phosphate by the cell.
pstS transcription is controlled at the level of transcriptional initiation and the pst operon transcript is differentially cleaved in the 5' direction to generate transcripts of different lengths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcription of the pstS gene is controlled by PhoP and that the pst operon contains a 3' untranslated region that is important for the regulation of its transcription.
